reason: The loose sand suggests the rover may need a traction aid, and metal stock plus cargo mesh seems useful for making one.
expectation: I expect a mesh-based crossing aid, though I don't know exactly what it will make.

alternatives.reason: Sieving gravel might also help prepare the crossing, but I want to try making a traction aid first.

effect: The panels need gravel to help support the rover over loose dust, so gathering suitable material is the next step.
reaction: The mesh frames holding gravel make physical sense, and I’m curious how the crossing will work.
reason: Sieving at the firm gravel patch is the only numbered action offered and seems useful for filling the traction panels.
expectation: I expect to obtain gravel suitable for the panels, though I don’t know exactly what the sieve will produce.

effect: The sieve produced coarse gravel, which appears ready to fill the traction panels.
reaction: That result is straightforward and fits the plan.
reason: The panels are designed to hold gravel, and this is the only numbered action offered.
expectation: I expect gravel-filled panels that can help the rover cross the loose sand.

effect: The gravel-filled tracks complete the crossing preparation. The result clarifies that the frames keep the supporting stones from spreading sideways.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the mesh frames and gravel form a practical support for the wheels.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the traction panels was most worthwhile because their design explained how they spread a wheel's weight and hold gravel over loose dust.

leastWorthwhile.text: Sieving the gravel was the least engaging passage: it produced the expected material without much further explanation.

surprise.text: I had expected a traction aid, but the raised frames holding gravel added a useful detail to how it would work.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary. Once the panels were made, the gravel and assembly steps had clear purposes, although each was the only numbered option offered at the time.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see the crossing and find out what the second ice core contains; this chapter ends with the tracks prepared.
